name: agent-cortex token map
description: Central mapping of capability names and kinds, paths, and agent naming conventions across the claude and pi harnesses. Single source of truth for install-time token substitution. See token-map.README.md for the design rationale.

token_format.decision: Adopt the {{CAPABILITY:name}} / {{PATH:name}} / {{SECTION:name}} grammar already standardised by ADR #63 (agents/README.md) rather than a dotted {{capability.name}} form. The uppercase type prefix disambiguates token kinds at a glance, keeps capability/path/section names in one namespace collision-free, and matches the token grammar skills are already written against. The type is CAPABILITY and not TOOL because a row may name a command: a token is not a promise that its argument is a model-callable tool.

types.CAPABILITY: {{CAPABILITY:<canonical capability key>}} — replaced at install time with the bound harness's name for that capability (see capabilities). Its kind is per harness: a `tool` may appear in a tool list, a `command` may not.
types.PATH: {{PATH:<path key or relative path>}} — replaced at install time with the harness-resolved path (see paths; a relative arg under skills/ is mapped onto the harness's staged shape first — see layouts).
types.SECTION: {{SECTION:<name>}} — replaced by the agent composer with <harness>/<name>.md section content. Not a global substitution; out of scope for token-map.json (see contract).

layouts.description: The tree each installer stages a resource into. `{{PATH:...}}` resolution reads it: a row is authored against the repository tree, so a harness that stages a resource in a different shape needs the row mapped onto its own. Only `skills` differs — Claude Code's plugin scan discovers `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` directly under `skills/`, so bin/installers/claude.mjs copies every skill flat and the group segment an authored row carries is dropped; bin/installers/pi.mjs preserves the repository grouping, so the row resolves as written.

sources.pi: agents/<name>/ composable dirs (canonical) — composed at runtime by the agent-modes extension
sources.claude: agents/<name>/ composable dirs (canonical) — composed by bin/installers/claude.mjs (install-time generator, the only generator — the generated claude/ plugin subtree is not committed)

wake.description: How each harness tells ralph that a background worker finished. `{{SECTION:wake}}` in agents/ralph/agent.md resolves to agents/ralph/<harness>/wake.md; this table is the machine-readable form of the same fact, so the mechanism is recorded rather than inferred from prose (see the wake table in agents/README.md).

notes.pi: Blocking wait: wait_for_agents returns as soon as one worker finishes, carrying its result inline. No timer to start, nothing to kill — there is no poll loop. Progress is read from the bead trail the worker writes (`bd show`, `bd provenance log`).
notes.claude: Event-driven: the harness re-invokes ralph when a worker completes and delivers the result inline. No poll timer and no sleep. Progress is read from the bead trail the worker writes (`bd show`, `bd provenance log`), never from a file ralph tails.

capabilities.rg: Canonical alias for grep. Claude and pi collapse it onto their single search tool (Grep / grep).
capabilities.glob: Claude has a dedicated Glob tool. pi's built-in pattern-search tool is find (hypa_find when the pi-hypa extension is installed).
capabilities.ask_user: Claude (AskUserQuestion) prompts the user mid-run. pi's equivalent is ask_questions, provided by the pi-questions package (an ordinary runtime dependency of this package that `agent-cortex install pi` bundles into the staged package's node_modules) — the genuine interactive-questioning tool, restoring grilling in plan/ralph-plan/strategy modes. Like fetch_content (pi-web-access), it is only present when its package is installed, so the mapping depends on that package (see the extension-manifests idea). pi still intentionally ships no permission popups; ask_questions is the interactive mid-run question tool, not a popup.
capabilities.web_fetch: pi's fetch_content comes from the pi-web-access package (an ordinary runtime dependency of this package that `agent-cortex install pi` bundles into the staged package's node_modules).
capabilities.skill: Claude (Skill) exposes skills as a tool. pi has no dedicated skill tool — skills are surfaced in the always-present 'Available skills' context block and loaded by reading the listed SKILL.md path ({{PATH:<skill>/SKILL.md}}). The pi mapping is read, the tool used to load a skill's file; a dedicated skill tool is a follow-on design candidate if prompting proves insufficient.
capabilities.read_agent: Claude's Task returns results inline — there is no separate read step, so read_agent drops on claude (null). pi exposes read_agent as a fallback to wait_for_agents.
capabilities.task: Claude provides a subagent tool natively. On pi it is supplied by this repo's own extensions/subagent extension (which also registers read_agent and wait_for_agents), not by pi itself — a pi session started before that extension was installed has no dispatch tool at all. Skills must therefore stop and report a missing subagent tool rather than improvising a backgrounded CLI run, which has no completion signal.
capabilities.wait_for_agents: PI-only blocking wait over background subagent runs (the task tool): returns the results of completed agents and STILL RUNNING for the rest. Claude's Task delivers results inline with no wait step — null on claude.
capabilities.peer_send: Session-to-session message send. pi takes it from the published pi-peer package (an ordinary package the consuming repository installs itself, never a dependency of this one). Claude Code has it built in and its docs name it there. Both address a peer by the name or address their own list reports, and neither send is proof of receipt. Only sends and discovery are tokenised: pi-peer's peer_get and peer_await have no Claude Code equivalent, and a null claude mapping drops the token and leaves the sentence that named it broken, so harness-varying prose must never name them — such passages stay inside a harness-labelled runbook.
capabilities.peer_list: Peer discovery: the peers that can receive a message, and the address each is reached by. pi's is the pi-peer package's tool. Claude Code's built-in equivalent is ListAgents (an earlier binary named it ListPeers), which also reports reachability and so doubles as the peer-state read.
capabilities.peer_get: The read half of the peer channel, pi-only: pi-peer's peer_get inspects a message, conversation or peer by id. Claude Code delivers a peer reply inline and has no equivalent, so the claude column is null and no claude tool set lists it. It is a tool-set row, not a prose row — prose must never tokenise it, for the reason recorded on peer_send: a null mapping would drop the token and leave the sentence that named it broken.
capabilities.peer_await: The wait half of the peer channel, pi-only: pi-peer's peer_await joins a send that returned pending, or one whose await window closed. Claude Code delivers the reply inline and has no equivalent, so the claude column is null. It is a tool-set row, not a prose row, for the same reason as peer_get.
capabilities.task_list: Claude Code's worker listing: the subagents a session has dispatched. The claude wake section names it, so the claude tool set lists it. pi has no listing tool — this package's subagent extension tracks workers through wait_for_agents and read_agent instead — so the pi column is null.
capabilities.task_get: Claude Code's worker read by id. Null on pi for the same reason as task_list: read_agent is pi's equivalent and already has its own row.
capabilities.task_stop: Claude Code's worker cancel. Null on pi, which cancels nothing because its wake mechanism is a blocking wait with no timer to stop (agents/ralph/pi/wake.md).
capabilities.post_merge_watch: Who waits for a CI run that outlives the check's own wait window. The row maps a name, not a protocol: the verdicts and the escalation rule layered above it are harness-invariant text, so only the mechanism is tokenised. pi's name is this package's own post-merge-watch extension, which re-runs the check on a timer and wakes an idle session with the verdict. Claude Code's is its built-in ScheduleWakeup tool, which schedules the session's own resumption so it can re-run the check. The values differ in kind — an extension on pi, a tool on claude — because that is what each harness supplies; the recorded kinds are `command` on pi and `tool` on claude, because the extension registers a CLI flag the user starts the session with and the model cannot call it, while ScheduleWakeup is model-callable. The surrounding prose therefore describes only what both do (the session resumes, the check runs again, the verdict table is unchanged) and never a call shape.
capabilities.idle_watch: Who wakes ralph while it runs, so a stalled worker or newly ready work reaches it without a human prompt. Consumed by agents/ralph/agent.md's Idle watch section, which names the row once and states the arming rule, the wake handling and the status line around it; skills/workflow/ralph/REFERENCE.md's Idle Watch section carries the detail. The row maps a name, not a protocol: pi's name is this package's own idle-watch extension's tool, which polls one configured check on a backing-off cadence for the life of the session and nudges the session with the ids that changed. Claude Code's is its built-in ScheduleWakeup tool, which schedules the session's own resumption so it can run the check again. Both are model-callable tools, unlike post_merge_watch, so the row also appears in ralph's per-harness tool lists. The surrounding prose therefore describes only what both do (the session resumes, the check runs again, and only a changed answer resumes it) and never a call shape — no parameter, no action name, and no statement of how the cadence is bounded, because pi's watch has no tick limit while claude's is the scheduled instant. The no-watcher fallback is plain prose in the same section, so it survives both renders.
capabilities.interrupt_rewind: How an interrupted task returns to its checkpoint and leaves the interruption behind. Consumed by agents/guppi/agent.md's interrupt protocol, which names the row once and states the checkpoint, record, rewind and resume steps around it. The row maps a name, not a protocol: pi's name is this package's own interrupt-bookmark extension's resume tool, which rewinds the session tree and has pi's summariser keep the abandoned branch under a branch summary labelled `interrupt`. Claude Code's is its built-in /rewind command, which restores the conversation and the file checkpoints taken for it. The values differ in kind — a model-callable tool on pi, a user-facing command on claude — because that is what each harness supplies. Constraints on the prose: it must describe only what both do (the session returns to the earlier point, and the interrupt's turns leave the live context) and never a call shape; it must also state who acts, because the actor forks with the kind — guppi performs the rewind where the harness gives it a tool, and hands it to the human where the harness gives it a user command; and it must not tokenise the checkpoint half, because Claude Code checkpoints on its own while pi needs a tool call, and a null claude column would drop the token and leave the sentence that named it broken. test/guppi-interrupt-render.test.mjs stages both installs to prove the fork.
capabilities.interrupt_checkpoint: The checkpoint half of the interrupt protocol, pi-only: guppi takes a resume point by calling this tool, while Claude Code checkpoints on its own with no tool to call, so the claude column is null and no claude frontmatter lists it. It is a tool-list row, not a prose row — prose must never tokenise it, for the reason recorded on interrupt_rewind.
capabilities.interrupt_resume: The resume tool as a tool-list row, for an agent that declares its tools per harness (guppi lists it in agents/guppi/pi/frontmatter.json). It is distinct from the interrupt_rewind prose row, which maps the same pi name to Claude Code's user-run /rewind: a tool list cannot carry /rewind, because the agent cannot call a user command, so the claude column is null and no claude frontmatter lists it.
capabilities.compact_window: How a stay treats the window. Consumed by agents/guppi/agent.md's Context lifecycle, which names the row once and states what a stay does to the window. The row maps a name, not a protocol, and its two values differ in kind — Claude Code's built-in /compact command on claude, this package's own session-transition extension's request_compact tool on pi — so the surrounding prose describes only what both do (the window is summarised and its recent tail is kept) and never a call shape. Neither side may be null: a null would drop the token and leave the sentence that named the mechanism short of a name. The row is a mixed-kind one for the same reason as post_merge_watch: that is what each harness supplies.
capabilities.flush_window: How a switch treats the window. Consumed by agents/guppi/agent.md's Context lifecycle, which names the row once and states that a switch drops the window and carries nothing across. The row maps a name, not a protocol, and its two values differ in kind — Claude Code's built-in /clear command on claude, this package's own session-transition extension's request_flush tool on pi — so the surrounding prose describes only what both do (the window is dropped, and nothing is carried into the replacement) and never a call shape. A flush carries no handoff on either harness: the replacement session is seeded with nothing, and the next session's own session start re-establishes the rubric and the queue. The row replaced clear_window, whose pi column was a session switch the model could not call; the row now names a tool on pi, so the rule can be acted on where it is stated.

paths.pi: plugin_root is the staged package `agent-cortex install pi` materialises at ~/.agent-cortex/pi; pi loads that directory by path and the shipped extensions resolve their own resources relative to it (agent-modes computes plugin_root from its actual install location). A checkout or symlinked install differs — installers compute plugin_root from the actual resolution and can override it (--plugin-root).
paths.claude: plugin_root stays ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} (env var) for the materialised plugin — never a literal ~/.agent-cortex/claude. Claude Code copies marketplace-installed plugins (including local directory sources like ~/.agent-cortex/claude) into its own cache and expands the env var per context, so a literal home path in substituted files would break under cache-copy; the installer passes the env form through verbatim.
paths.skill_anatomy: A path entry whose relative path sits under docs/ names a document the install ships: both installers copy it from the package root into the staged tree at that relative path (scripts/lib/docs.mjs), so a skill can read it on a machine with no checkout. One copy per install serves every skill that references it — write-a-skill and refactor-skill both do. The repo's docs/ stays the single source of truth; the staged copy is a verbatim copy, never a second authored version.

agents.prefix: Claude strips the agent-cortex: name prefix during conversion (NAME_PREFIX in bin/installers/claude.mjs): pi agents are agent-cortex:<slug>, claude agents are <slug>.

contract.summary: Installers substitute {{CAPABILITY:...}}, {{PATH:...}}, and {{SECTION:...}} tokens in generated harness files using this map. This contract is the single reference installers must implement; token-map.json is the data those rules operate on.
contract.binding: The harness id is the same value the installer is invoked with (agent-cortex install <harness>). Each harness reads its own column from the capabilities, paths, and agents sections.
rules: CAPABILITY: replace {{CAPABILITY:<key>}} with capabilities.<key>.<harness>.name. Canonical keys are exact, case-sensitive strings (the names the canonical sources in agents/<name>/agent.md are authored with).

CAPABILITY kind: every row value is either null or an object {name, type} whose type is `tool` or `command`. The kind is per harness, because the same capability genuinely differs between them (interrupt_rewind is a pi tool and a claude command). A string value is invalid — there is no shorthand.
CAPABILITY tool: a `tool` is model-callable and may appear in a tool list.

CAPABILITY command: a `command` is invoked directly by the user or agent (a slash command, or an extension's command). It may appear in rendered prose and must never appear in a tool list — a tool-list context that resolves to a `command` is a hard error naming the canonical key, never a silent omission.

CAPABILITY null: a null value means the harness has no equivalent. In prose, remove the token (and emit a warning). In a tool-list context (frontmatter tools: [...]), omit the entry. Do not substitute an empty string.

CAPABILITY unknown: a {{CAPABILITY:<key>}} with no entry in capabilities is a hard error — the map must be extended. This mirrors the generators (bin/installers/claude.mjs, bin/installers/pi.mjs), which throw on unknown capabilities.
PATH named key: replace {{PATH:<key>}} with the resolved value of paths.<key>.<harness>.

PATH relative skill: a relative arg whose first segment is `skills` is authored against the repository tree, which nests every skill at skills/<group>/<name>/<file>. Map it onto the harness's staged shape from layouts.skills.<harness>: `grouped` keeps it as written, `flat` drops the group segment (skills/<name>/<file>) because that installer copies skills flat. An arg with fewer than three segments is a hard error — no install has a skill one level under skills/.

PATH resolution: a value may be a literal string, an ${ENV_VAR} token, or a {base, relative} spec. Resolve {base, relative} by joining relative onto the resolved base. Leave ${ENV_VAR} values verbatim — the harness expands them at runtime (claude's ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}).
PATH unknown base: a {base, relative} spec whose base is not a key in paths is a hard error.

SECTION: {{SECTION:<name>}} is resolved by the agent composer from <agents_dir>/<harness>/<name>.md; token-map.json does not substitute it. Installers must leave SECTION tokens untouched for the composer.
Contract version: installers must reject token-map.json versions higher than the contract version they implement.
Case sensitivity: all token arguments and map keys are case-sensitive.

error_handling.unknown_capability: throw — the map must stay complete
error_handling.unknown_path_base: throw — the map must stay complete
error_handling.null_capability_in_tool_list: omit the entry from the array
error_handling.command_in_tool_list: throw, naming the canonical key — a command is not a tool and omitting it silently would hide the defect
error_handling.unsupported_version: throw with the supported version range
